question.question: Does the PrepareReply transport preserve the producer-established value ballot for the same acceptor and instance, so recovery receives the context used to rank retained support?
question.importance: Losing the value ballot can mis-rank command and dependency history during authority transfer. The local transport obligation is independent of the previously confirmed phase-reporting defect; global safety impact is a potential consequence.
contexts: Nonzero producer-established value ballot with higher Prepare promise
event_paths: handlePrepare -> replyPrepare -> SendMsg/Marshal -> New/Unmarshal -> recovery input

question.trigger_rationale: S_prepare copies inst.vbal into PrepareReply; S_recover_select ranks replies by VBallot; S_prepare_codec omits this field while S_prepare_new zero-initializes the receiver. A small actual-message path with value ballot 1 directly discriminates preservation without needing a global recovery scenario.

obligation.description: A successfully serialized and decoded PrepareReply must preserve the value ballot copied from the acceptor local instance by handlePrepare, for the same acceptor, instance and Prepare request. Recovery must receive that value-history context unchanged across the message transport boundary.

scope.description: Value-ballot fidelity at the PrepareReply transport boundary under an actual producer-derived local history.
assumptions: Non-Byzantine messages and successful codec completion
No concurrent producer mutation during observation
excluded: Crash/restart, timer deadlines and eventual client completion

grounding.derivation: handlePrepare explicitly copies local inst.vbal into the reply separate from the promise ballot. The registered Serializable interface and sender/receiver call chain transfer that object; handlePrepareReply uses VBallot to rank retained values. Therefore successful reply transport owes equality of this semantic field with the producer local value ballot for the same report. This is a local preservation duty from actual producer and consumer, not an assumed protocol theorem or arbitrary serialization of unused state.
grounding.applicability: An implementation-produced PrepareReply is serialized through SendMsg and decoded into the registered fresh message type; compare the local value ballot copied by handlePrepare with the corresponding decoded report.
unresolved: Global recovery consequence is not claimed.
alternatives: Other fields and local coordinator history can remain correct despite this field loss.

feedback.answered: The accepted status witness remains a confirmed local phase-reporting violation: its actual value ballot was zero, so it does not test codec preservation. New source investigation shows handlePrepare copies local vbal while PrepareReply codec omits it and New returns fresh zero state. The current check isolates the transport field using a proposal-established nonzero ballot. The map now distinguishes local tuple, constructed report and decoded input; it no longer implies faithful export of vbal.
